overview: The Council addressed a persistent rat infestation at a private apartment complex and advanced a zoning amendment to allow fractional affordable housing payments. Significant decisions included approving several litigation settlements and passing a ban on face surveillance technology on its third reading.

items.title: Retirement of Library Director Barbara Kerr
items.summary: Approved a resolution congratulating Barbara Kerr on her retirement after 40 years of service and requested the Library Trustees name a space within the library in her honor.

items.title: Approval of Records
items.summary: Tabled the records of the March 24 meeting and approved the records of the March 31 special joint meeting.

items.title: Committee Report: Snow Removal and Litigation
items.summary: Approved the April 1 report of the Committee of the Whole regarding city snow removal efforts and litigation matters discussed in executive session.

items.title: Grant of Location: 3960 Mystic Valley Parkway
items.summary: Approved a National Grid petition to relocate a utility pole and remove existing structures at Commercial Street, subject to several conditions from the Engineering Division.

items.title: Licence Approval: Cilantro's Mexican Grill
items.summary: Approved a common victualler license for the business at 495 Riverside Avenue with extended operating hours until midnight, subject to a 90-day review period.

items.title: Rat Infestation at Brooks Park Apartments
items.summary: Approved a resolution to engage the landlord and the Board of Health regarding an ongoing rat infestation and requested information on potential enforcement actions and citations. Residents testified about severe hygiene issues and the presence of rodent waste and carcasses on the property.

items.title: Zoning Amendment: Fractional Affordable Housing Payments
items.summary: Referred a proposed zoning ordinance to the Community Development Board that would allow developers to make fractional payments to the Affordable Housing Trust Fund rather than rounding up the number of required affordable units. The change aims to remove the disincentive for developers to build just below unit thresholds.

items.title: Tabling of Items
items.summary: Tabled two items for consideration at a special meeting to be scheduled the following week.

items.title: Litigation Settlements
items.summary: Approved eight settlement amounts recommended following an executive session, including $235,000 for Joseph P. Cardillo and Son Inc. and $19,000 for Convoy.

items.title: Board and Commission Appointments
items.summary: Confirmed four appointments to the Elections Commission to ensure the processing of nomination papers and approved appointments to the Conservation Commission, Garden Commission, and Zoning Board of Appeals.

items.title: Appropriation: Election Pole Pads
items.summary: Approved a $13,800 appropriation from the Capital Stabilization Fund for 20 new election pole pads.

items.title: Face Surveillance Ban
items.summary: Approved the third and final reading of an ordinance banning face surveillance technology in the city.

items.title: Public Participation
items.summary: Residents spoke regarding the international significance of May Day and expressed concern over the city's limited enforcement tools for private property rat nuisances.
